blockers.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-render-gpu/tests/gpu_plan.rs:3328 (assert); kernel src/kernel.wgsl:361 threshold_apply compares hsk_lum(rgb) >= t - 0.5/255
blockers.diagnosis: lattice pixel (129, 0) = (r, g, b) = (7/16, 10/16, 0); with hsk_lum = 0.3 r + 0.59 g + 0.11 b (kernel.wgsl:50-51, verified) its luminance is exactly 0.5 = 127.5/255, the threshold-128 boundary; Vulkan binary32 evaluation lands just below it (black), dx12 and pigment on or above (white). A boundary-sensitive comparison, not a port defect; kernel.wgsl is outside this lane path list; the tolerance is not widened (lead rule)

deviations_for_lead: GpuClientPort has two methods beyond the brief: authorize(&GpuGrant) (called before every submission, so a superseded, settled or revoked grant never submits across any port: GUI-DESKTOP-036) and counters() (closed counters, rule 5)
SettleOutcome adds Abandoned (drop without release); Settlement adds native_driver (always Unknown here) and in_flight (a settlement with work in flight is refused InFlight and changes nothing)
GpuError gains Denied(DenialCode) (additive; at the pigment port BackendError::Unavailable(grant_*))
GrantLedger is public (issue_host, rebind_host, revoke) so a host port and the tests can implement GpuClientPort outside render-gpu
SharedDevice backend reacquire no longer opens a render-gpu device: it is DeviceLost (recovery is the host's); no caller in harness-view or harness

GpuContext::acquire/acquire_next removed (not pub(crate)): the transient adapter opens leases (device::acquire_lease) and the backend builds the context on the lease (GpuContext::from_lease); unused pub(crate) functions would be dead code
